title: Ohm's Law and Resistance
notes: **Ohm's law.** At constant physical conditions (temperature, state) the potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current: V ∝ I, or V = IR.
**Resistance and resistivity.** R = ρL/A: resistance grows with length L and falls with area A; resistivity ρ (unit Ω·m) is a property of the material itself.
**Temperature dependence.** For metals R_t = R_0(1 + αt) with α > 0; semiconductors have negative temperature coefficient as carrier density rises with heat.
**Conductance and conductivity.** Conductance G = 1/R (siemens) and conductivity σ = 1/ρ; better conductors have large σ and small ρ.
**Limitations.** Ohm's law does not hold for diodes, electrolytes, superconductors or conductors at changing temperature — there V–I is not a straight line through the origin.

Resistance depends on the piece of wire: it is resistivity times length over area. Resistivity depends on the material. Stretching a wire makes it longer and thinner, so its resistance rises even if the resistivity does not.

**Ohm’s law and resistance factors (classified)**

| Factor | Effect on R | Formula role |
|---|---|---|
| Length L | Doubles when L doubles | R ∝ L |
| Area A | Halves when A doubles | R ∝ 1/A |
| Resistivity ρ | Material property | R = ρL/A |
| Temperature | Metals: R rises | ρ(T) increases |

**Ohmic vs non-ohmic behaviour**

| Behaviour | V–I graph | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Ohmic | Straight line through origin | Metals at constant T |
| Non-ohmic | Curved | Diode, filament lamp, thermistor |

subtopics.name: The law
points: Resistance is the opposition to current flow, measured in ohms
Ohm's law is empirical, not a fundamental law of nature

subtopics.name: Resistivity
points: R = rho L / A, where rho is resistivity, a material property
Resistivity depends on material and temperature, not on shape
Resistance depends on both material and geometry

subtopics.name: Temperature dependence
points: For metals, rho increases with temperature: rho = rho_0 (1 + alpha dT)
For semiconductors, resistivity DECREASES with temperature as more carriers are freed
This opposite behaviour distinguishes metals from semiconductors

subtopics.name: Ohmic versus non-ohmic
points: Ohmic conductors give a straight V-I line through the origin
Non-ohmic devices (diodes, filament lamps, thermistors) give curved or asymmetric graphs
A filament lamp's resistance rises as it heats

subtopics.name: Microscopic origin
points: Drude model: electrons accelerate in the field and lose momentum in collisions
R = rho L/A follows from I = nAev_d and v_d = eE tau/m
Explains why longer, thinner wires have more resistance

subtopics.name: Superconductivity
points: Below a critical temperature some materials drop to zero resistance
Persistent currents flow without energy loss
Used in MRI magnets and maglev systems
